title: Cold-chain and last-mile vaccine logistics in low-resource settings
bottleneck: Many vaccines require continuous refrigeration from factory to arm, but cold-chain infrastructure is absent across rural Africa and South Asia, and health-worker shortages compound the problem. Thermostable formulations exist for few vaccines, and redesigning biologics for heat stability is slow and expensive.
why_it_blocks: The last mile is where vaccine equity dies: doses expire in warehouses while unvaccinated populations remain vulnerable, allowing variants to emerge and prolonging every pandemic.
current_state: Solar-powered cold chain and controlled-temperature-chain pilots have expanded, but most novel vaccines (including mRNA) still need stringent cold storage. Thermostable platform research is underfunded relative to discovery. Microneedle patches and spray-dried thermostable formulations could bypass refrigeration entirely, but reformulating each vaccine is a multi-year regulatory undertaking with thin commercial incentive.
